gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-mono: Nordic's strokes never thin out, a single brushed width with dabs of space between the letters. Noto Sans Mono takes over with tall, generously spaced lowercase and open curves, a plain sans that lets the heading's tight folds stand out.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-mro:
Nordic looks ancient and powerful, with strokes of constant width.

Noto Sans Mro follows in sans-serif form, its words dense and tall through the middle, so a long passage feels compact and steady under that heading.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-multani: Nordic carries a powerful, ancient feel, drawn with one constant line width and spaced like scattered brush dabs. And Noto Sans Multani offers the strongest single quality here: a lofty x-height with a gap-toothed e, modern and quietly open.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Noto Sans Myanmar lays down a heavy-looking strip of text, its c opening broad and welcoming beneath the heading. Nordic, bent-wire constant and tightly folded, gives it a closed, ancient counterweight.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Chiselled and ancient, Nordic holds its curves at full thickness right through every turn. And Noto Sans Nabataean, a sans-serif with lowercase standing almost cap-tall, works well when the heading is sized noticeably larger.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-nandinaga: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Nandinagari, with short ascenders, a big lowercase body and openings that stay generous at every weight. Nordic, with zero stroke modulation, sits above it as the hard-edged, ancient voice.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-newa:
Modern and open, Noto Sans Newa shows a clear mouth on its lowercase e.

Nordic pulls the other way, with cramped, folded letters and a powerful monoweight stroke, so the page has a tight headline and a spacious text.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-nushu:
Contemporary lines define Noto Sans Nushu, with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke.

Nordic earns its keep when big and short, where its monoweight, vertical and horizontal strokes of identical weight, look ancient and powerful.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Nordic is built from a single constant stroke, with dabs of space between its cramped, closed-up letters. Noto Sans Ogham does the opposite: bold-looking, tall lowercase and wide gaps in the e.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Noto Sans Ol Chiki reads as solid blocks of words, its curve tails held well back from the body. Under Nordic's constant pen width, the text would feel tidy and unhurried.
